title: bitNot
definition:
Performs a bitwise NOT operation on a numeric value.
A bitwise NOT inverts each bit of the binary representation of the number.
For each bit position:
- If the bit is 1, it becomes 0
- If the bit is 0, it becomes 1
This operation is commonly used when working with bit flags, permissions or encoded values to invert stored states.
Example :
5 = 0101
~5 = 1010 → -6 (depending on integer representation)

title: bitAnd
definition:
Performs a bitwise AND operation between two numeric values.
A bitwise AND compares the binary representation of two numbers bit by bit.
For each bit position:
- If both bits are 1, the result is 1
- Otherwise, the result is 0
This operation is commonly used when working with bit flags, permissions or encoded values, where multiple states are stored inside a single integer.
Example :
5 = 0101
3 = 0011
bitAnd = 0001 → 1

title: bitOr
definition:
Performs a bitwise OR operation between two numeric values.
A bitwise OR compares the binary representation of two numbers bit by bit.
For each bit position:
- If at least one bit is 1, the result is 1
- If both bits are 0, the result is 0
This operation is commonly used when working with bit flags, permissions or encoded values, where multiple states are stored inside a single integer.
Example :
5 = 0101
3 = 0011
bitOr = 0111 → 7

title: bitXor
definition:
Performs a bitwise XOR (exclusive OR) operation between two numeric values.
A bitwise XOR compares the binary representation of two numbers bit by bit.
For each bit position:
- If the bits are different, the result is 1
- If the bits are the same, the result is 0
This operation is commonly used when working with bit flags, permissions or encoded values, where multiple states are stored inside a single integer.
Example :
5 = 0101
3 = 0011
bitXor = 0110 → 6

title: bitShiftLeft
definition:
Performs a bitwise left shift on a numeric value.
This operation shifts the binary representation of a number to the left by a specified number of positions.
Each shift to the left adds a 0 to the right, effectively multiplying the number by 2 for each shift.
Example :
5 = 0101
<< 1
bitShiftLeft = 1010 → 10

title: bitShiftRight
definition:
Performs a bitwise right shift on a numeric value.
This operation shifts the binary representation of a number to the right by a specified number of positions.
Each shift to the right removes the rightmost bit, effectively dividing the number by 2 for each shift (ignoring any remainder).
Example :
5 = 0101
>> 1
bitShiftRight = 0010 → 2
